The test image shows a single corn plant that is completely wilted and brown/tan, with dried, curled leaves throughout the entire plant, while all surrounding plants remain healthy and green. This systemic whole-plant wilt pattern is very distinctive.

The Goss's wilt reference image (top-left panel) matches almost perfectly — the same pattern of tan/brown wilted leaves throughout the entire plant standing out dramatically among healthy green neighbors. This is classic Goss's wilt (bacterial wilt caused by *Clavibacter michiganensis* subsp. *nebraskensis*), which causes systemic vascular wilt leading to complete leaf firing and browning of the whole plant.
